description.text: Throughout the woods and hills of Yinquan are countless warm and soothing hot springs which draw visitors from across Yanshen and beyond, as the aching folk of Haless, from peasants to nobles, come to relax in their healing waters.
description.text_en: Throughout the woods and hills of Yinquan are countless warm and soothing hot springs which draw visitors from across Yanshen and beyond, as the aching folk of Haless, from peasants to nobles, come to relax in their healing waters.

description.text: Our nation was founded by lost and destitute peasants who had left their hovels to find a better home. When they entered the Mulim, they were guided through its woods, and directed by the fox spirits known as Huli Jing to dig in specific areas, ultimately revealing the hot springs for which our land is widely known. Since then, the Huli Jing have protected Yinquan from the shadows, gathering around springs and shrines devoted to them, and many of our people keep foxes as pets out of respect for our trickster guardians.

description.text: The thick and confusing mists of the Mulim have confounded armies for eons, even restricting navigation by magical means. Our people have been embraced by the woods though, and quickly learned how to traverse the Mulim with ease. Some have even learned how to gather and harness the mists to shield our soldiers when on the march.

description.text: Liho was the most influential of the Huli Jing in guiding our nation in its early years, and it is said that she continues to live among us, leading us even now. Liho's Maidens are her closest and most devout followers, performing rituals and performances across Yinquan and diligently maintaining the countless shrines dotted throughout the Mulim.

description.text: Harimar had heard of the springs of Yinquan long before he ever even entered Yanshen, and when he reached us he visited the largest of them all, enjoying himself to such an extent that he left a garrison of his warriors to defend it to ensure he could visit in perpetuity. More than a thousand years later, the same spring would be visited by the Phoenix Emperor himself, Jaher, and the prestige of the area, now known as Conqueror's Spring, increased even further.

description.text: The waters of Yinquan are known to loosen more than tired muscles - officials from neighboring lands tend to speak far more openly in our baths than they would normally, and we have eyes and ears willing to pass information along to our leaders.

description.text: While Yanshen burns under the heels of warlords and conquerors, Yinquan has always been a land of peace and tranquility, where merchants of even warring nations can relax and trade in peace. We benefit from this serene atmosphere, finding lucrative trade opportunities from our visitors.

description.text: While initially a title dedicated to the Mulim forest, where it is said that shrines outnumber the trees, Lingyuk has earned the epithet "Land of Ten-Thousand Shrines". Encouraged by the spirit-revering government, shrines of countless kinds have popped up across Haless. Dedicated to all manner of spirits big and small (especially the Huli-Jing), the Mystic Accord has rocketed upwards in popularity - almost as if the people of Haless were waiting for the moment to proclaim their true faith!

description.text: All spirits are revered as protectors and mentors, but none more so than Huszien Herself. Already the leader of Yinquan, the realm which finally took up the mantle of uniting spirit-kind, She was a natural candidate to lead all of Lingyuk. Her reconstructed form is a veritable wellspring of magic; wed to Yanhe, She has at Her disposal an almost inconceivable amount of power. Huszien is loath to use it. After all, She does not need magic to steer the nation to greatness. When She does use it, however, even the mountains bend to the decrees of Lingyuk.

description.text: Huszien might rule the nation, but Her composite spirits rule Her. The Huli-Jing and the Gumiho, the aspects of Her existence, regularly gather together to debate how best to process the world around Huszien. This is known as the Endless Debate. Whoever is dominant in these debates influences Huszien's personality, advising Her to act one way or another even as she comes to her own conclusions. A unique arrangement like this has given Huszien and the ruling class a number of very important lessons on how to reach a consensus. Using those lessons, more minority groups can be placated without compromising the unity of Lingyuk.

description.text:
Haless has been forced away from its natural state for millennia. The High Temples, constructed by some loathsome batch of precursors, all but banished spiritkind from the continent. Separated from our brethren for so long, we have all but forgotten the truth of this land.

Nevermore! Lingyuk, the spirit domain, shall excise the rot that has set in; we declare war against all the false "nations" of Haless. Once their divisions have been washed away with blood, the continent shall return to the state it should have always been in: Man and spirit, co-existing in eternal harmony.

description.text: The Maidens of Liho are an organization that dates back centuries. First patronized by Yinquan, they have since grown to encompass the entirety of Lingyuk's state. They practice a unique style of magic that makes heavy use of ritualized dances and the now well-known gohei staff. This magic serves to purify our weapons, ensuring that they always strike true. Our armor, meanwhile, seems all the more willing to suffer otherwise destructive blows after being imbued with Huszien's power.

description.text: Second only to Huszien is Yanhe, the Great Dragon. As he is the husband of Huszien, it is his duty to ensure that Her children are as well cared for as his. In this regard, Yanhe is generous; The Yanhe river is always welcome and friendly to the children of Lingyuk. Its waters are especially fertile, quick to rejuvenate the soil along its bank. Our farmers are able to produce great harvests with no extra effort - all through our harmony with the spirits.

description.text: Yinquan's rich history of festivals, encouraged by the Huli-Jing, has proven contagious. Many of their holidays and celebrations have spread throughout Lingyuk, leading ultimately to the creation of a single, unified calendar. These celebrations are incredibly frequent, and during them men and spirit mix without any care for the identity of others. It is here that the harmony of Lingyuk can be seen in full display. All of the merriment has led to a much happier populace, too.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you only want a lighthearted fox nation or dislike waiting, province-specific requirements, complex prerequisites, and unavoidable political purges.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Unify northern Yanshen and build hot-spring pilgrimage income, follow Holi, Huszien, and the Rending chain, then form Lingyuk, appease every Great Spirit, and expand across Yanshen, Rahen, and Vímdaal.
player_overview.overview: Yinquan begins as a folk fantasy of hot springs, rice wine, shrines, fox spirits, and the mage Holi. Recover the homeland, investigate the High Temples, reassemble Huszien, and deliberately trigger the Rending. After forming Lingyuk, the campaign becomes Great Spirit appeasement, Halessi conquest, and a Maiden revolution; land reform and human-spirit coexistence quickly join massacres, purges, forced submission, and extermination of resisters.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy fox-spirit folklore, very long connected stories, magic and spirit mechanics, dramatic country transformations, and late-game conquest.
signature_features: Investigate the High Temples and revive Huszien from spirit fragments, deliberately triggering the Rending early.
Complete Great Spirit demands, appease spiritual beings, and unlock spirit armies.
Form Lingyuk from Yinquan and continue through land revolution, class purges, and human-spirit unification.
player_overview.tagline: From a hot-spring fox-spirit republic to spirit-world ascendance, remake Haless through Maiden theocracy and Great Spirit power into a cruel utopia.

reasons: The charming folk opening contrasts sharply with a dark theocratic endgame.
Huszien’s revival and the deliberate Rending make a world-scale mechanism part of the national story.
Great Spirit appeasement, spirit armies, and the sacred marriage offer unusual spiritual gameplay.
The 51-mission Y26-to-R86 campaign has clear stages and very long late-game goals.
warnings: Some Great Spirit demands cannot be previewed and may require waiting or temporary occupation.
The late game requires sustained conquest across several regions.
The Maiden storyline includes massacres, class purges, forced conversion, and extermination.

positive_indicators: A stated ideal of human-spirit coexistence
values.rationale: The early route centres on spirit protection, coexistence, folk construction, and public reform. After Lingyuk forms, power centralises and political purges, forced unification, and extreme violence appear; the result is an escalating trajectory rather than a static label.
red_flags: Extreme violence against groups refusing the new order
